root_cause_label: Incorrect install.packages version-pinning syntax triggered uncontrolled source build without system prerequisites, causing harness timeout cascade and repeated no-op polling that left the run unresolved despite eventual technical success.
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent used the unsupported version argument in install.packages without first installing BLAS/LAPACK/gfortran prerequisites, triggering a long uncontrolled source build that timed out and devolved into repeated empty-command no-op polling steps, ultimately preventing a clean harness-visible completion despite the underlying task artifacts being correctly produced.
t_err_evidence: install.packages('rstan', ...) omits required system deps; exit code -1, times out
t_commit_evidence: Once the uncontrolled source install started under a 120-second harness timeout without prerequisites, the trajectory was locked into a cascade of timeout-driven no-op polling steps (steps 6-15 are all empty commands with exit -1), making clean harness completion impossible. Even though the agent eventually fixed system deps at step 18 and re-ran sampling, the repeated polling pattern and reliance on passive timeout observation meant the harness marked the run as unresolved.
t_surface_evidence: cannot find -llapack ... -lblas ... -lgfortran ... compilation failed for package 'RcppEigen'
trigger_explanation: The agent lacked knowledge that base R's install.packages does not support version pinning via the version= argument (requiring remotes::install_version instead), and also lacked awareness that RStan's compilation requires system-level BLAS/LAPACK/gfortran to be pre-installed. Both gaps caused the initial installation attempt to be fundamentally misconfigured.
